reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address passive film formation on Q235 steel, temperature-dependent oxidation kinetics, or film morphology in NaCl solution. E1 discusses Mn and Cr dissolution in molten fluoride salts for HEAs and 316H stainless steel; E2 studies CoCrFeNiTix HEA coatings on Q235 in NaCl but focuses on Ti content effects, not temperature or bare Q235 film formation. The key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: Q235 steel forms a passive iron oxide film in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution
At room temperature, slow oxidation yields a dense, adherent, protective oxide film
At elevated temperature (~70°C), rapid oxidation yields a porous, cracked, nonprotective oxide film
Film integrity controls corrosion rate: protective film suppresses, defective film accelerates degradation
Temperature is the dominant variable governing film formation kinetics under fixed chloride/oxygen conditions
